title: Scaling properties of same-family on-policy distillation
data_curation: A controlled math setup with no new data. Students are Qwen2.5 Base models (0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, 7B, 14B) first SFT'd on a subset of Dolci-SFT (300K samples per epoch, 2 epochs) for chat-template instruction following. Teachers are obtained by GRPO on the mixed GSM8K + MATH training split of 14.8K examples; OPD reuses the same prompts. The 'gold score' is accuracy on the mixed GSM8K/MATH test split of 6.3K examples, on which teachers and students are both evaluated. The off-policy cold-start condition uses one epoch of SFT on teacher rollouts over 20K Dolci-Think-RL prompts; pure off-policy distillation (OffPD) uses 5 teacher responses per training prompt for 5 epochs.
curriculum: Each model follows SFT -> GRPO RL (teacher) or SFT -> OPD (student). The grid has 25 Vanilla-OPD teacher-student pairs (weak-to-strong, same-base, strong-to-weak) and 17 Delta-OPD pairs. Each OPD run is at most 10 epochs (580 updates). Design-choice studies compare pure OPD, an off-policy SFT cold start followed by OPD, and pure OffPD. Bootstrapped chains apply RL only to the 0.5B model and then distill upward stage by stage (e.g. 0.5B -> 1.5B -> 3B -> 7B -> 14B), each stage's best OPD checkpoint becoming the next teacher (5 Vanilla and 3 Delta chains).
method: An empirical scaling study of OPD in the style of Gao et al.'s reward-overoptimization laws. Vanilla-OPD uses the sampled-token, zero-discount advantage log pi_T - log pi_theta; Delta-OPD uses the teacher's RL shift log pi_T - log pi_T^base plus a reverse-KL penalty to the student's SFT reference (the shared core of OPD2, Direct-OPD and W2S-OPD). Training progress is indexed by d = sqrt(k3), the token-mean reverse KL from the student initialization. Linear fits G = c + m*d on the first 30 (Vanilla) or 40 (Delta) checkpoints define the useful-transfer slope m; the transfer endpoint is where the curve leaves the 95% predictive band for 3 consecutive checkpoints. Joint power laws are fitted: 1 - G_peak = A N_S^-alpha (N_T^eff)^-beta (1 - G_T^eff)^zeta, and a matching law for m, with teacher size capped at student size. A local Fisher-geometry argument explains why gain is linear in sqrt-KL. All runs use verl v0.8.0; OPD LR 1e-6 constant, batch 256, max rollout 2048; teacher GRPO group size 8, no KL penalty, single seed per run.
eval_metrics: Gold score (held-out GSM8K+MATH test accuracy, sampled at temperature 1.0, max 2048 tokens), peak gold score G_peak, initial slope m, transfer extent d_transfer, and a logged teacher-induced proxy score P. Linear early fits reach R^2 0.932-0.988 with slopes 0.175-0.721. Law quality is judged by leave-one-scale-out RMSE and outer-scale extrapolation RMSE. Vanilla joint law: A=0.97, alpha=0.30, beta=-0.27, zeta=0.95, leave-one-scale-out RMSE 1.66 points vs 3.43 for a size-only law; Delta: zeta=1.01, beta=-0.33, RMSE 0.82. Peak grid example: 14B student reaches 77.7% (0.5B teacher) to 87.3% (14B teacher); 0.5B student peaks at 40.8% with a 3B teacher but 37.7% with a 14B teacher.
key_results: In every weak-to-strong pair the student's peak exceeds its teacher's score, and the joint law extrapolates to the held-out largest student and teacher within 0.7 (Vanilla) and 0.4 (Delta) accuracy points; it also predicts a score-matched intermediate 3B teacher's 7B-student peak at 74.1 vs observed 73.8, correctly ranking it below the 1.5B teacher (77.5). Delta-OPD has a larger matched-KL slope in 15 of 17 pairs; an off-policy cold start costs 6.6/15.7/19.4 points for 3B/7B/14B students under the 0.5B expert; every bootstrapped chain peaks below direct OPD from the 0.5B expert (e.g. 76.8 vs 77.7 at 14B).
evolution_note: The paper carries the scaling-law method of Gao et al. (2023) for RLHF reward overoptimization, and its direct-alignment extension, over to on-policy distillation (GKD, MiniLLM, Thinking Machines' OPD) and its teacher-shift variants (OPD2, Direct-OPD, W2S-OPD). It turns weak-to-strong OPD from a one-off trick into a predictable tool: peak capability can be estimated from student size, capped teacher size and teacher score before training, which supports training RL expertise once at small scale and transferring it across a family. It also overturns the bootstrapping gain reported by Burns et al. (2024) for this setting. Evidence is limited to one family (Qwen2.5), one math mixture, 2K-token responses and single seeds.
